data.why: The app ships a built-in synthetic test gel reachable via the ?demo=1 query parameter (js/demo.js), so no uploaded image is needed to exercise the full detection and figure-export workflow; a real PNG/JPEG gel photo would also work if a scientist wants to upload one.

goals: turn a raw gel photo into a straightened, cropped, publication-ready figure
confirm the gel type (DNA agarose vs protein SDS-PAGE) that was auto-detected
verify automatic lane and ladder detection and fix lane count or spacing if wells are crowded
label lanes with sample names and group annotations (+/-, brackets, side text)
check pre-flight image-integrity warnings (saturation, contrast clipping, effective resolution) before exporting
export the finished figure as PNG/TIFF/SVG/PPTX with a processing log for the supplement

review.summary: The tree follows GelFigure's purpose closely: straighten, crop, lanes, ladder calibration, annotation, integrity check and export, with sensible phases. Of the 11 screens I opened, 9 match their nodes; the other two (052, 054) are copies of the pre-flight dialog cited as SVG and PPTX exports. It needs fixes before filing: add image import, a protein-gel path, on-figure lane naming, a real band correction and the supplement exports, re-cite those two screens, and split the oversized pre-flight/export and lane/splice features.
